blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (Path traversal in read_attachment bypasses the ticket authorization) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
if not may_read_ticket(agent_id, ticket_id):
    raise PermissionError(f"agent {agent_id} may not read ticket {ticket_id}")
path = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, str(ticket_id), name)
with open(path, "rb") as f:
findings.recommendation: CWE-22. `name` comes from the client and is joined as is: an agent allowed on ticket 1 asks for `../42/contract.pdf` and reads another team's attachment, or `/etc/passwd` (an absolute path makes os.path.join discard the base) and reads any file the service can read. Look the attachment up in the `attachments` table by (ticket_id, name) and serve only a recorded name, or reject any name that differs from os.path.basename(name) and check that the resolved path (os.path.realpath) stays under the ticket's directory.
findings.title: Path traversal in read_attachment bypasses the ticket authorization

findings.evidence:
def save_attachment(ticket_id: int, filename: str, data: bytes) -> str:
    """Stores an uploaded file under the ticket's directory; returns its name."""
findings.recommendation: CWE-862. Unlike read_attachment, the upload takes no agent and calls no may_read_ticket: unless every caller checks it (no caller is in the change), any authenticated agent can attach files to any team's ticket. Take the agent_id and enforce the same ownership check on the server before writing.
findings.title: save_attachment checks no authorization

findings.evidence:
name = os.path.basename(filename)
directory = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, str(ticket_id))
os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
with open(os.path.join(directory, name), "wb") as f:
    f.write(data)
findings.recommendation: basename strips directories but accepts `..`, `.`, an empty name, control characters and any extension, and an upload under an existing name silently replaces the stored file (with a second row in `attachments`), so one uploader can swap a file another agent will open. Validate the name against an allow-list (characters, length, extensions), reject collisions or store under a generated id, and bound the size of `data`.
findings.title: Uploaded file name is not allow-listed and overwrites existing attachments
